searchText: Yeah, I realized this fairly recently; turns out the better approach would be to use an exponential formula (or a reasonable alternative is the second-degree Taylor approximation: `new_base_fee = old_base_fee * (1 + ((block_size - target)/target) / 8 + ((block_size - target)/target)**2 / 128`) How do you define "recent"? 😛 I believe you told me about the current formula being lopsided because it is a first degree taylor approximation something like ~~6 months ago~~ 3 months ago... 3 months ago is still less than 10% earlier in the EIP 1559 progressbar, which started in 2017 😆 oh btw EIP 1559 also increases throughput slightly because the long-run-average gasused will now be *exactly* the target, instead of being 1-5% (or whatever it is now) below the limit Aside from "changing the formula", what would this entail? If we can show it's better, and don't have to re-do all the analysis/simulation/testing/etc. then we probably should? but if it changes some adjacent properties of the EIP and will require a ton of new testing, then I think maybe we wait and ship 1559 as is?
